title: Kāmo ’kārṣīt, manyur akārṣīt

words.gram: s-aorist, 3rd sg. active (the svara sign is S’s)

sandhi.rule: -aḥ + a- becomes -o ’- (the a elided, marked by avagraha)
a visarga after u becomes r before a vowel

translation.literal: Desire did (it); anger did (it). Salutation, salutation.
translation.readable: It was desire that acted, it was passion that acted — salutation, salutation.

meaning: A one-line confession said with a bow: whatever wrong has been done was done by desire and by anger, not by the self. It abbreviates two expiatory formulas of the Mahānārāyaṇa (10.61 kāmo ’kārṣīt … and 10.62 manyur akārṣīt …), where each is spelled out at length (‘desire acts, not I; desire is the doer, not I’). The rite keeps only their first words and the salutation.
in_the_rite: Step samasti-abhivadana, after the salutation to all the deities and before the abhivādana, in all three services.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: The full formulas are Mahānārāyaṇa 10.61 (79) and 10.62 (80) in this site’s edition (/upanishads/mahanarayana/).

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: akārṣīt before manyuḥ and before namaḥ ends in n: a final t becomes n before a nasal. S marks the svara of akārṣīt with ᳚, which the padaccheda keeps as printed.
